premises: Phase-selective recrystallization can fully recrystallize the soft FCC phase while retaining the hard B2 skeleton in a eutectic HEA.
Recrystallizing the FCC phase eliminates weak boundaries and dislocation pile-ups at FCC/B2 interfaces.
Eliminating pile-ups reduces stress concentrations, microcracking, and premature failure.
The resulting microstructure increases uniform elongation to ~35% and true stress to ~2 GPa.
Semi-coherent phase boundaries in the as-cast eutectic HEA are strong and accommodate high stress.
